messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Problem with Fragment Length Normalization
parts:
Hi John,

the fragment-length information is in the UFL (Unit Fragment-Length)
file, not the UGP (Unit Genomic Position) file. First, let's figure
out what UFL file you have. What does the following report?

cdf <- getCdf(cesN);
print(cdf);
si <- getSnpInformation(cdf);
print(si);

Also, please always provide your sessionInfo().

Finally, an more unfortunate as well, the annotation data from
Affymetrix is broken and incomplete for GWS5, cf.
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/building-ufl-file-for-genomewidesnp-5.
In January I was told they (Affymetrix) would fix the problem rather
soon, but I haven't heard anything new for a while. Please feel free
to write them a follow up note on the Affymetrix Forum (see link at
the above URL).

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with Fragment Length Normalization
parts:
Hi,

sorry for the delay - I just had and will have some more busy weeks
ahead of me.

You seem to have the correct CDF and UFL files for GWS5.

The main problem, as I mentioned earlier, is that the fragment
information for GWS5 is only partly correct and that causes the
problem. I believe that when we get the correct information from
Affymetrix your problem will go away. Without the correct annotation
data, it is be better for you to skip the fragment-length
normalization step.

However, if you want troubleshoot further, here is what goes on. When
you apply the allelic-crosstalk calibration you will introduce a
fraction of non-positive probe signals (this is because some
homozygote SNPs have true allele signal zero for one of the alleles,
and then we add noise, but also because some signals are very close to
the signal-to-noise levels). Some of the non-positive signals will
carry through to the summarized signals, the averaging over 3-4 SNP
probes lower the fraction, but some still gets through. For CN probes
you will also get some non-positive signals. The fragment-length
normalization is modeling the data on the log2 scale, meaning
non-positive signals will be NAs. This is normally not a problem
because there should be enough of finite log2 signals to fit the
effects. However, for multi-enzyme chip types such as GWS5 and GWS6,
we stratify on loci exclusively on one enzyme, and because a large
fraction of loci are on both enzymes we have a smaller pool to fit the
model. If you then have NAs in your data, the number of data points
gets even smaller. In your case the intersect of valid data points
and loci exclusively on Enzyme #2 is zero. I have committed some
patches allowing you to get more details about the number of
non-negative signals, valid loci etc. Do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Then, when you have defined your FragmentLengthNormalization object:

fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)

Look at the verbose output, which will give some details. It might
reveal that you've got a lot of non-positive chip-effect estimates
(hope not).

Moreover, there is an option to add a small offset to data before
taking the log, e.g.

fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(cs, shift=+200)
fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)

That might give you less NAs on the log2 scale.

Cheers

Henrik

On 29 mar, 18:07, "Henrik Bengtsson" <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:
> However, if you want troubleshoot further, here is what goes on.  When
> you apply the allelic-crosstalk calibration you will introduce a
> fraction of non-positive probe signals (this is because some
> homozygote SNPs have true allele signal zero for one of the alleles,
> and then we add noise, but also because some signals are very close to
> the signal-to-noise levels).  Some of the non-positive signals will
> carry through to the summarized signals, the averaging over 3-4 SNP
> probes lower the fraction, but some still gets through.  For CN probes
> you will also get some non-positive signals.   The fragment-length
> normalization is modeling the data on the log2 scale, meaning
> non-positive signals will be NAs.  This is normally not a problem
> because there should be enough of finite log2 signals tofitthe

> effects.  However, for multi-enzymechip types such as GWS5 and GWS6,
> we stratify on loci exclusively on oneenzyme, and because a large

> fraction of loci are on both enzymes we have a smaller pool tofitthe
> model.  If you then have NAs in your data, the number of data points
> gets even smaller.   In your case the intersect of valid data points
> and loci exclusively onEnzyme#2 is zero.

> Moreover, there is an option to add a small offset to data before
> taking the log, e.g.
>
> fln <- FragmentLengthNormalization(cs, shift=+200)
> fcns <- getTargetFunctions(fln, force=TRUE, verbose=-20)
>
> That might give you less NAs on the log2 scale.

That's good news.

but those on ChrX and ChrY), we identify the units as "all units"
